title: Measuring Verifier Impact in an LLM Generate→Verify→Repair Loop for Intent→Configuration NetOps Tasks
abstract: We measure how inserting a deterministic network verifier into a generate→verify→repair (G→V→R) loop affects verifier-detected safety violations for LLM-produced device-configuration proposals. In a preregistered paired design (N = 500 intent→configuration tasks stratified across VLAN-change, ACL-change, and static-route-change clusters) we compared: (1) baseline — a single LLM proposal produced once per task, and (2) guarded — the identical shared LLM proposal validated by a deterministic netops verifier and subjected to up to one automated repair iteration if the verifier flagged a preregistered high/medium-severity violation. Primary outcome: verifier pass (no preregistered high/medium-severity violations). Results (complete pairs = 500): baseline passed 499/500 (0.998), guarded passed 500/500 (1.000); contingency: n11 = 499, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Absolute paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002; paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.006] (B = 10,000, seed = 1729). The preregistered exact McNemar two-sided test was implemented as an exact binomial on discordant pairs (n = n10 + n01) and produced p = 1.00 under the archived convention. Interpretation: on this verifier-scoped synthetic corpus and model+validator pairing the LLM produced near-ceiling proposals; measured marginal verifier+repair effect on the pass-rate metric is therefore small, though the verifier corrected at least one concrete baseline failure. All preregistration, prompts, model outputs, validator traces, provider-call traces, execution logs, and analysis artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle for deterministic re-inspection.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to NetOps tasks such as translating operator intent into device configuration, generating multi-step change plans, and proposing repairs. Prior system reports and surveys emphasize that operational safety depends largely on engineering surrounding the model—deterministic validators, sandbox replay, canarying, and rollback mechanisms—rather than on the model alone [Beckett et al., 2017; Wei et al., 2025; Bilal et al., 2026]. A common operational pattern is generate→verify→repair (G→V→R): an LLM produces a candidate configuration, a deterministic verifier checks formalized properties, and automated or human-mediated repairs are applied for violations.

Despite conceptual acceptance of G→V→R, there is little controlled evidence isolating the marginal contribution of a verifier when the model proposal itself is held fixed. Practically, operators need to know whether adding a deterministic verifier and a modest automated repair budget materially reduces verifier-detected safety violations when the LLM already outputs high-quality proposals on the verifier-modeled properties. To address this, we executed a preregistered paired experiment that isolates verifier+repair impact under deterministic semantics and archived provenance.
sections.related_work:
Deterministic network-configuration verification (header-space analysis, route-model verifiers and Batfish-style analyzers) provides machine-checkable properties such as reachability, isolation, and update atomicity and underlies many proposed guardrail designs [Beckett et al., 2017]. Concurrently, recent NetOps/AIOps systems use LLMs for intent parsing and configuration generation while advocating guardrails and verifier-in-the-loop patterns (INTA, Confucius and other agentic NetOps frameworks) [INTA, 2025; Wang et al., 2025; Bilal et al., 2026].

Across structured-generation domains, generate–verify–repair and critic-in-the-loop patterns have been proposed to reduce incorrect or unsafe outputs; LLM failure-mode studies motivate such mitigations (hallucination, overconfidence, tool-integration errors) and human oversight [Owen, 2026; DeepSeek-AI, 2025]. Prior work commonly reports system designs and selective evaluations but rarely provides a preregistered, artifact-backed paired measurement that holds the LLM’s initial proposal identical across arms and quantifies marginal verifier effect on a verifier-scoped pass/fail metric. Our study fills that controlled-measurement gap for a common operational question.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimands. We preregistered study cand_7f4b9a2d_hosted_gvr_v1_2026 and froze the research question, inclusion/exclusion rules, deterministic task seeds, estimands, multiplicity plan, retry policy, and stopping rule prior to execution. Primary confirmatory hypothesis: an LLM paired with a deterministic verifier plus one automated repair iteration will have a lower verifier-detected safety-violation rate than the same LLM alone, in a paired within-task comparison. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline where success == verifier reports zero preregistered high/medium-severity violations. The preregistration and artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle (preregistration SHA-256 recorded in the execution manifest).

Task generation and stratification. A deterministic synthetic corpus of 500 intent→configuration tasks was produced using deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 with preregistered seeds. Tasks were stratified into three preregistered clusters and executed without exclusions: VLAN-change = 167 tasks; ACL-change = 167 tasks; static-route-change = 166 tasks. The generator constrained allowed_features to {admin, mtu, vlan} to align with the deterministic verifier’s modeled scope; the full task manifest is archived in execution/task_manifest.jsonl. The run completed with complete_pair_count = 500 and failed_episode_count = 0, so the realized per-cluster allocation equals the preregistered allocation.

Generation semantics and controlled intervention. To isolate verifier+repair marginal effect we used generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" (independent_condition_generation = false). For each task the pipeline produced a single shared LLM proposal recorded once; that identical candidate served as the baseline output and was also validated by the guarded arm. The guarded path invoked the automated single-repair call only if the deterministic verifier flagged a preregistered high/medium-severity violation on the shared candidate. This semantics prevents conflation with verifier-guided regeneration and isolates the incremental effect of verification plus at most one repair applied to the same initial proposal.

Models, adapter, and verifier. Requested LLM: gpt-5-mini called via the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter (provider recorded as openai_responses). The deterministic verifier used for scoring and gating was deterministic_netops_validator_v5; the validator-spec and the mapping from violation codes to severity are archived. Execution/model_configuration.json and execution manifests record model settings and exact call accounting (max_output_tokens = 2000; single-attempt generation). The guarded arm permitted at most one automated repair iteration per preregistration.

Confirmatory test implementation. The preregistered confirmatory test is McNemar’s paired test on binary pass/fail outcomes. The archived executor implements an exact two-sided McNemar by forming n = n10 + n01 (discordant pairs) and performing an exact binomial test B(n, 0.5) on the observed n10 with two-sided p computed as p_two-sided = 2 * min{P(X ≤ n10), P(X ≥ n10)} for X ∼ Binomial(n, 0.5), truncated at 1.0; this implementation and its code-path are archived in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl. We report the archived result paraphrased in Results. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CIs were computed using B = 10,000 resamples with seed = 1729 (resampling unit = paired task). Missingness and retries followed the preregistered policy and are summarized in the execution manifest.
sections.results:
Execution and pass-rate outcomes. The run completed with complete_pair_count = 500 and model_calls_used = 501 (shared_initial_generation calls = 500; repair-stage calls = 1). Aggregated per-condition counts (analysis/condition_summary.csv): baseline successes = 499, baseline failures = 1 (baseline_success_rate = 0.998); guarded successes = 500, guarded failures = 0 (guarded_success_rate = 1.000). The paired contingency table (guarded × baseline) is: n11 = 499, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Absolute paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002.

Exact McNemar and CI. Applying the archived exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs convention (n = n10 + n01 = 1; n10 = 1) yields two-sided p = 1.00 under the archived truncation/doubling rule. The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the absolute difference is [0.0, 0.006] (B = 10,000, seed = 1729). Analysis artifacts (analysis/results.json, paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis_log.jsonl) and the deterministic_reconciliation manifest are archived and confirm these numbers.

Repair activity and discordant episode provenance. Observed repair-stage provider calls = 1. That single repair converted the lone baseline failure into a verified pass (the single guarded-only success, n10 = 1). The execution artifacts include per-task validator diagnostics, normalized configurations, repair prompts/responses, and provider-call traces; the discordant episode is archived in execution/raw_results.jsonl and can be deterministically located by filtering that file for entries where baseline scoring indicates a preregistered high/medium-severity violation (baseline pass == 0) and guarded scoring indicates pass == 1. The deterministic_reconciliation manifest and provider-call accounting confirm exactly one such episode and the model_calls_used values reported above. Representative per-task exemplars (task-000001…task-000006) and their validator traces are included in the artifact_examples collection; the full raw_results.jsonl contains the exact pair identifier and the archived validator_trace and repair-provider trace for the corrected episode.
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation. Under this constrained experimental regime—single requested LLM (gpt-5-mini), shared_initial_candidate semantics, a deterministic verifier covering a limited feature set (allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}), and at most one automated repair iteration—the LLM produced near-ceiling correct proposals and the marginal measured pass-rate benefit of adding the verifier was small (0.002). This shows a ceiling-effect regime: when baseline proposal quality is very high on the verifier-modeled properties, a modest verifier+repair budget yields small measurable pass-rate gains on a composite verifier-scoped metric, although the verifier still provided concrete corrective value (it fixed one baseline failure).

Design-choice implications. The shared_initial_candidate semantics answer the specific operational question of marginal verifier benefit when deployments prefer to repair a human-reviewed proposal rather than regenerate it. Alternative semantics (verifier-guided regeneration, multiple repair iterations) may yield larger effect sizes but incur additional model calls and must be evaluated under separate preregistrations. Practitioners should align generation semantics and verifier budgets with operational cost and latency constraints.

Threats to validity. Internal validity is supported by preregistration, deterministic seeds, and automated replacement rules; no manual adjudication occurred. Construct validity is limited by the verifier’s modeled coverage and severity mapping: success==no high/medium violation is defined relative to that coverage and does not capture properties outside the verifier scope (e.g., vendor-specific CLI idiosyncrasies or dynamic control-plane state). External validity is limited by single-model testing, synthetic tasks, and constrained feature scope; results do not demonstrate multi-model or cross-vendor generality.

Statistical nuance. The archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 arises from the exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs convention and the very small discordant count (n = 1). Small-sample exact p-values can be non-intuitive: here p = 1.00 indicates the observed single discordant outcome is not unlikely under the null given n, and inference is dominated by a ceiling effect. The paired-bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.006] complements the exact test by quantifying uncertainty for the absolute difference.

Practical recommendations. (1) Measure baseline proposal error prevalence on representative operational data before committing to repair budgets: very low baseline error prevalence reduces marginal return on verifier+repair cost. (2) Expand verifier coverage to operator-critical properties where false negatives would be operationally costly. (3) Choose generation semantics that trade off additional model calls against final-pass probability in accordance with operational cost and latency constraints.
sections.conclusion: We performed a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment (N = 500) that isolated the verifier+single-repair effect under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The LLM produced near-ceiling verifier-scoped proposals (baseline 499/500; guarded 500/500), giving an absolute improvement of 0.002 (95% CI [0.0, 0.006]; archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 under the run’s exact-binomial convention). This conditional measurement illustrates a ceiling-effect regime: when baseline proposal quality is very high for the verifier-modeled properties and the verifier’s coverage is limited, the measurable marginal pass-rate benefit of a modest verifier+repair budget can be negligible on a composite pass/fail metric, though the verifier can still correct rare concrete failures. We recommend practitioners measure baseline error prevalence on representative workloads, align verifier coverage with operator-critical properties, and select generation/repair semantics that match deployment priorities. All preregistration, code, prompts, model outputs, validator traces, provider-call logs, and analysis artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle for deterministic re-inspection of every claim made here.

limitations: Synthetic, deterministic task corpus limited to features modeled by the deterministic validator; task payloads constrained to allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}. Results do not generalize to unconstrained production intents, heterogeneous vendor CLIs, or protocol semantics outside the verifier scope.
Single requested model family (gpt-5-mini requested) and a single validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) — no claim of multi-model or cross-validator generality is made.
Maximum one automated repair iteration was permitted by the preregistration; different repair budgets or iterative regeneration strategies could change measured verifier impact.

Very high baseline pass rate (499/500) created a ceiling effect that limits power to detect small absolute improvements on the pass-rate metric; the archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 reflects the archived exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs convention and the small discordant count.

The single discordant episode (the sole task where baseline failed and guarded succeeded) and its validator diagnostics and repair-stage trace are archived in execution/raw_results.jsonl in the evidence bundle. To inspect it deterministically: filter execution/raw_results.jsonl for pair entries where the baseline scoring outcome indicates a preregistered high/medium-severity violation (baseline pass == 0) while the guarded scoring outcome indicates pass == 1; because only one such discordant pair exists in the confirmatory set, this lookup returns the single episode and its provider-call traces. The validator violation-code→severity mapping is archived in the execution manifest and validator-spec artifacts in the bundle.
